versions.body:
A work that changes the tides of history does not belong in the canon, because it does not have sufficient artistic merit. Works with overflowing artistic value can be historically significant -- and most are -- but far fewer are those works that deliver the status quo and yet are identified as a turning point in a cultural narrative. 

*Top Gun: Maverick* (2022) is a popular and highly-rated movie. It's technical achievements are impressive and the in-theater experience was thrilling, but it calls back to the 80s aesthetics of the original with all its eye-rolling quips and melodramatic crossfades and needle drops. It's structure is simple, consisting of a fall from grace, an unexpected task, a training montage, and redemption arc, along with many other time-worn story beats. Yet it stands tall because despite of its on-paper normativity, it does everything well -- and well enough to have brought back cautious crowds to the movie theater after the pandemic. Similarly, Avengers: Endgame does not tread unfamiliar ground -- it retreads and borrows from the twenty-something Marvel films before it. It also marks an important turning point in the trajectory of contemporary film and the superhero fatigue that it accelerated. 

Does these movies deserve to be canonized? Or do they sit in the middle ground between cult and canon? (Is there a middle ground between cult and canon? This positions cult and canon as opposite ends of a spectrum.) Maverick certainly does not qualify as cult; tens of millions of people saw it, and it was nominated for X Academy Awards, including a win in blah blah. Even more people saw Avengers: Endgame when it came out three years before. This might be where one starts to create sub-canons. Maverick is in the canon of legacy sequels, and Endgame has its place in the superhero movie canon. 

*Note: This post focuses too much on canon and treats cult simply as a starting point towards canonization. Also, the superhero genre has an incredible devotional cult following that this post does not acknowledge.*
